dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef001
dependency_coverage.meaning: The dependent type of admissible step-data packages for fixed dimension, filter, scale, matrix, right-hand side, and iteration. By constructor D020 and projections D002-D011, it packages six vector-valued functions, four real-valued functions, and the stated residual, update, error-bound, nonnegativity, convergence, and asymptotic-comparison properties.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The conclusion is universally quantified over every inhabitant of this type, so all packaged step assumptions are available, but existence of such an inhabitant is not asserted.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef002
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its second vector-valued field, denoted correctionHat.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the correction vector c_t appearing as A c_t in the exact identity and in the admissible-step residual bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef003
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its fifth vector-valued field, denoted deltaR.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the residual perturbation δr_t in the exact identity and is constrained by the step's residual-perturbation bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef004
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its sixth vector-valued field, denoted deltaX.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the update perturbation δx_t and contributes A δx_t to the exact identity.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef005
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its seventh field, the real-valued function epsilonR.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its value εr_t bounds the residual perturbation, is nonnegative, tends to zero along l, and appears in the coefficient εr_t+εu_t+ω_t in the final bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef006
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its eighth field, the real-valued function epsilonU.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its value εu_t bounds the update perturbation, is nonnegative, tends to zero along l, and appears in the coefficient εr_t+εu_t+ω_t in the final bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef007
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its tenth field, the real-valued function omega.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its nonnegative value ω_t appears in the admissible-step residual bound and in the final coefficient εr_t+εu_t+ω_t; no convergence of ω_t is required.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef008
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its fourth vector-valued field, denoted residualHat.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The exact conclusion contains residualHat_t explicitly, while the step assumptions identify it with b-Ax_t+δr_t.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef009
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its ninth field, the real-valued function w.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: Its nonnegative value w_t multiplies the current residual norm in both the admissible-step residual bound and the final eventual bound; no convergence of w_t is required.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef010
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its first vector-valued field, denoted xHat.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the current approximate iterate x_t whose residual norm appears on the right side of the final estimate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef011
dependency_coverage.meaning: For a step package, this is its third vector-valued field, denoted xHatNext.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It is the next approximate iterate x_t^+, appearing in the exact identity, the left side of the final residual estimate, and the size term involving its norm.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef012
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef012 n is the type of real n-by-n matrices, represented as functions Fin n → Fin n → Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes A as a square real matrix of dimension n.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef013
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef013 n is the type of real n-vectors, represented as functions Fin n → Real.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It fixes b and every vector-valued step component as elements of R^n, with pointwise vector operations.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef014
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef014 l scale lhs rhs means that there exists a real-valued remainder r with r=O_l(scale²) such that eventually along l, lhs(t) ≤ rhs(t)+|r(t)|.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expands the second conclusion into an existential quadratic-order remainder and an eventual residual-norm inequality. It also occurs among the admissible-step assumptions for comparing successive iterate norms.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef015
dependency_coverage.meaning: This is the norm of A supplied by the Frobenius normed-ring structure, namely the Frobenius matrix norm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the factor ||A||_F multiplying the norm of the current or next iterate in the step assumptions and final bound.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef016
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef016 A states that the linear map x ↦ Ax on R^n is bijective.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It restricts the theorem to matrices whose matrix-vector action is injective and surjective.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef017
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef017 A x is the matrix-vector product Ax, with component (Ax)_i = Σ_{j∈Fin n} A_{ij}x_j.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines every occurrence of A applied to an iterate, correction, or perturbation.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef018
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef018 A b x is the residual b-Ax.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It defines the current and next residual vectors whose Euclidean norms occur in the step assumptions and final estimate.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef019
dependency_coverage.meaning: For x∈R^n, LocalDef019 x is sqrt(Σ_{i∈Fin n} x_i²), the Euclidean 2-norm.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It turns residuals, perturbations, b, and iterates into the exact scalar norms used by all inequalities.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef020
dependency_coverage.meaning: This constructor builds an admissible step from functions x_t, c_t, x_t^+, rHat_t, δr_t, δx_t, εr_t, εu_t, w_t, and ω_t satisfying: rHat_t=b-Ax_t+δr_t; x_t^+=x_t+c_t+δx_t; ||rHat_t-Ac_t||_2≤w_t||b-Ax_t||_2+ω_t(||b||_2+||A||_F||x_t^+||_2); ||δr_t||_2≤εr_t(||b||_2+||A||_F||x_t||_2); ||δx_t||_2≤εu_t||x_t^+||_2; all four scalar coefficients are nonnegative; εr and εu tend to zero along l; and, up to an O_l(scale²) remainder, eventually ||x_t||_2≤||x_t^+||_2.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It supplies the full set of assumptions carried by every quantified step package and determines the meanings of all projected fields.

dependency_coverage.name: LocalDef021
dependency_coverage.meaning: LocalDef021 l scale r states Asymptotics.IsBigO l r (t ↦ scale(t)²).
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It requires each remainder in LocalDef014 to be of order scale² along l.

dependency_coverage.name: And
dependency_coverage.meaning: Logical conjunction.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The theorem concludes both the pointwise exact identity and the eventual asymptotic residual estimate.

dependency_coverage.name: Eq
dependency_coverage.meaning: Propositional equality of two terms of the same type.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It expresses the exact vector identity in the conclusion and the exact residual and update identities in the step assumptions.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter
dependency_coverage.meaning: A filter on an index type, representing a limiting or eventual regime.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: The arbitrary filter l determines convergence, eventual truth, and all big-O statements.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.NeBot
dependency_coverage.meaning: The proposition that a filter is not the bottom filter.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It excludes the degenerate filter under which every proposition would hold eventually.

dependency_coverage.name: Filter.Tendsto
dependency_coverage.meaning: Tendsto f l₁ l₂ means map f l₁ ≤ l₂, i.e. f tends along l₁ to the regime represented by l₂.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It states that scale tends to 0 and, within an admissible step, that εr and εu tend to 0 along l.

dependency_coverage.name: Fin
dependency_coverage.meaning: Fin n is the finite index type consisting of natural numbers strictly below n.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It indexes the n vector coordinates and both dimensions of the n-by-n matrix.

dependency_coverage.name: HAdd.hAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: The addition operation selected by the relevant HAdd instance.

dependency_coverage.name: HMul.hMul
dependency_coverage.meaning: The multiplication operation selected by the relevant HMul instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It denotes ordinary real multiplication in scalar bounds and entrywise real multiplication inside matrix-vector products.

dependency_coverage.name: HSub.hSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: The subtraction operation selected by the relevant HSub instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It denotes pointwise vector subtraction in residuals and the exact vector identity.

dependency_coverage.name: LT.lt
dependency_coverage.meaning: The strict-order relation selected by an LT instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: With the natural-number instance, it expresses the hypothesis 0<n.

dependency_coverage.name: Nat
dependency_coverage.meaning: The natural numbers.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: They provide the dimension n and the otherwise unrestricted iteration parameter.

dependency_coverage.name: Ne
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ne a b means not a=b.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It imposes the hypothesis that b is not the zero vector.

dependency_coverage.name: OfNat.ofNat
dependency_coverage.meaning: Interpretation of a natural-number literal in a type with the corresponding OfNat instance.
dependency_coverage.effect_on_target: It interprets the literal 0 as natural zero, real zero, or the zero vector as required.

dependency_coverage.name: Pi.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Addition of functions is defined pointwise.

dependency_coverage.name: Pi.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Subtraction of functions is defined pointwise.

dependency_coverage.name: Pi.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The zero function has value zero at every input.

dependency_coverage.name: PseudoMetricSpace.toUniformSpace

dependency_coverage.name: Real
dependency_coverage.meaning: The real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instAdd
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary addition on the real numbers.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instMul

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instSub
dependency_coverage.meaning: Ordinary real subtraction, defined as addition of the additive inverse.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.instZero
dependency_coverage.meaning: The ordinary real number zero.

dependency_coverage.name: Real.pseudoMetricSpace

dependency_coverage.name: UniformSpace.toTopologicalSpace

dependency_coverage.name: Zero.toOfNat0

dependency_coverage.name: instLTNat

dependency_coverage.name: instOfNatNat

dependency_coverage.name: Finset.univ

dependency_coverage.name: Function.Bijective

dependency_coverage.name: HPow.hPow

binders: For every type ι and every filter l on ι equipped with a proof that l is not the bottom filter.
For every real n-by-n matrix A, real n-vector b, natural-number parameter iteration, and function scale:ι→R.
For every admissible step package indexed by l, scale, A, b, and iteration, with fields x_t, c_t, x_t^+, rHat_t, δr_t, δx_t, εr_t, εu_t, w_t, and ω_t.
hypotheses: The map x↦Ax from R^n to R^n is bijective.
b is not the zero vector.
For every t, εr_t≥0, εu_t≥0, w_t≥0, and ω_t≥0.
εr_t and εu_t tend to 0 along l.
There exists q:ι→R with q=O_l(scale²) such that eventually along l, ||x_t||_2≤||x_t^+||_2+|q_t|.
conclusions: There exists a function ρ:ι→R satisfying ρ=O_l(scale²) such that eventually along l, ||b-Ax_t^+||_2≤w_t||b-Ax_t||_2+(εr_t+εu_t+ω_t)(||b||_2+||A||_F||x_t^+||_2)+|ρ_t|.
mathematical_definitions: R^n is represented by functions Fin n→R, and real n-by-n matrices by functions Fin n→Fin n→R.
The residual at x is res(x)=b-Ax.
||A||_F is the matrix norm furnished by the Frobenius normed-ring structure, equivalently the standard Frobenius norm.
The step notation is x_t=xHat(t), c_t=correctionHat(t), x_t^+=xHatNext(t), rHat_t=residualHat(t), δr_t=deltaR(t), δx_t=deltaX(t), εr_t=epsilonR(t), εu_t=epsilonU(t), w_t=w(t), and ω_t=omega(t).
The asymptotic inequality relation used in the conclusion means existence of one such remainder ρ followed by an inequality holding eventually along l.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For any positive dimension, any nonbottom limiting filter, any scale tending to zero along that filter, any real square matrix whose matrix-vector action is bijective, and any nonzero right-hand side, every admissible inexact step satisfies two claims simultaneously. First, its next-iterate equation gives the exact pointwise vector identity Ax_t^+-b=(δr_t+Ac_t-rHat_t)+Aδx_t. Second, the Euclidean norm of the next residual is eventually bounded by w_t times the current residual norm plus (εr_t+εu_t+ω_t) times ||b||_2+||A||_F||x_t^+||_2, up to the absolute value of an existential remainder of order scale(t)² along the filter.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The theorem requires n>0. For n=0 the implication is vacuous because that hypothesis is false.
The filter is arbitrary apart from being nonbottom; ι need not be the natural numbers and no sequential or temporal structure is assumed.
The scale may have either sign and may vanish; only convergence scale→0 and big-O relative to scale² are required.

The conclusion is universal over admissible step packages but does not assert that any such package exists. If the constructor assumptions are inconsistent for particular data, the universal statement over steps is vacuous.
The exact vector identity holds for every t, whereas the residual-norm estimate holds only eventually along l.
The remainder in the final estimate is existential, may depend on all quantified data and the step, and is constrained only by being O_l(scale²); no sign or explicit formula is imposed.
Although εr and εu tend to zero, no convergence-to-zero condition is imposed on w or ω.
The iterate-norm comparison is itself only an eventual inequality with a separate existential O_l(scale²) remainder.
The iteration parameter is unrestricted and has no explicit role in either conclusion beyond indexing the step type; no relation between different iterations is encoded.
No convergence of x_t or x_t^+, no existence or approximation of an exact solution, no contraction factor, no condition number, and no forward-error bound are asserted.
Bijectivity of A and nonzeroness of b are hypotheses, but the conclusion does not explicitly mention an inverse matrix, determinant, singular values, or a normalized residual.
